passages.title: The School Garden
paragraphs: Last spring, the students at Midori High School started a small garden behind the gym. At first, only five students joined the project. They planted tomatoes, cucumbers, and sunflowers, and they took turns watering the plants every morning before class.

In July, the tomatoes were ready to pick. The students gave some of them to the school cafeteria, and the cooks used them to make a special salad. Many students who had never visited the garden tried the salad and became interested in the project.
Now more than thirty students take care of the garden. The club leader, Aya, says, "Growing food takes time and patience, but it also brings people together."

passages.title: A Message in a Bottle
paragraphs: When Ken was ten years old, he wrote a short letter, put it in a glass bottle, and threw it into the sea near his grandfather's house. In the letter, he wrote his name, his address, and a simple question: "Where will this bottle go?"

For years, nothing happened, and Ken almost forgot about the bottle. Then, when he was sixteen, he received a postcard from a woman in Canada. She had found the bottle on a beach while she was walking her dog.

Ken and the woman began to exchange emails. She told him about life in her small town, and he told her about his school in Japan. Ken now says that the bottle taught him that the world is both very large and surprisingly small.

passages.title: Why We Yawn
paragraphs: Almost everyone yawns several times a day, but scientists still do not fully understand why. One popular idea is that yawning helps to cool the brain. When we open our mouths wide and take a deep breath, cool air may lower the temperature of the blood that goes to the brain.
Yawning is also contagious. If you see someone yawn, you are likely to yawn too. Interestingly, this happens more often between family members and close friends than between strangers.
Some researchers think that this shows yawning may be connected to empathy, the ability to understand how other people feel. However, more studies are needed before we can be sure.

passages.title: The Paradox of Choice
paragraphs: Many people believe that having more choices always makes us happier. If a supermarket offers fifty kinds of jam instead of five, customers should be more satisfied, because each person is more likely to find exactly what he or she wants. Surprisingly, however, research suggests that this is not always true.

In a well-known experiment, shoppers were shown either a small display of jams or a large one. The large display attracted more attention, but the people who saw the small display were far more likely to actually buy something. When there were too many options, people found it hard to decide, and many simply walked away.

Psychologists call this the "paradox of choice." Having too many options can cause stress, because we worry that we might not choose the best one. Even after we make a decision, we may keep wondering whether another choice would have been better.

This does not mean that choice is bad. Rather, it suggests that there is a point beyond which more options stop helping us. Knowing this, we can make our lives easier by limiting our choices when a decision is not very important.

passages.title: Sleep and Memory
paragraphs: Students often stay up late before an exam, believing that every extra hour of study will improve their score. Yet a growing body of research shows that cutting sleep may actually harm learning. Sleep is not simply a time when the brain rests; it is also a time when the brain is busy organizing what we learned during the day.

During deep sleep, the brain appears to replay new information and move it from short-term to long-term memory. In one study, two groups of students learned a list of words in the evening. One group slept normally, while the other stayed awake all night. When both groups were tested two days later, the students who had slept remembered significantly more words.
Lack of sleep also affects attention. A tired student may read the same page three times without understanding it, which wastes the very time that staying up was supposed to save.
Of course, sleep cannot replace studying. The point is that study and sleep work together: we build knowledge while awake, and we store it while asleep.

passages.title: Robots in the Classroom
paragraphs: In some schools, small robots now help teach languages. The robots can repeat words as many times as a student needs, never lose their patience, and keep a record of each student's progress. Supporters argue that such machines allow teachers to spend more time on activities that only humans can do well, such as leading discussions.

Critics, on the other hand, worry that students might come to rely too much on machines. Language, they point out, is more than a set of words and rules; it is a way of sharing feelings and ideas with other people. A robot may correct your pronunciation, but it cannot truly understand why you want to say something.

Interestingly, a study in one elementary school found that students who practiced with a robot became more willing to speak in front of their classmates. The researchers suggested that making mistakes in front of a robot felt less embarrassing, so the students gained confidence before speaking to real people.
Perhaps the question is not whether robots should replace teachers, but how the two can work together.

written.modelAnswer: I think high school students should be allowed to use smartphones in class. First, they can quickly look up information they do not understand. Second, they can use useful learning apps to review lessons. However, students should follow rules so that they are not distracted. (49 words)

rubric.point: 最初に自分の立場（賛成・反対）をはっきり書いている
理由を2つ、First / Second などで区別して書いている
理由に具体的な内容（例・効果）がある
時制・主語と動詞の一致・冠詞などに大きな誤りがない
50語程度の分量になっている

questions.prompt: 意見文で、自分の意見と反対の考えにふれてから反論するときに使う表現は？
questions.explanation: 「〜と言う人もいるかもしれないが…」で反対意見にふれ、but のあとで反論する（譲歩→反論）。説得力が増す。

questions.prompt: 理由を追加するときの表現として最も適切なものは？
questions.explanation: In addition / Moreover / Besides で理由を追加。On the other hand は対比、As a result は結果、However は逆接。

questions.prompt: 英文の要約として最も適切なものは？
questions.sentence: Several studies have compared reading on paper and on screens. When readers were asked about details and the order of events, those who read on paper tended to do better. Researchers think the physical feel of pages helps readers build a mental map of the text.
choices: Reading on paper helps people remember details better than reading on screens.
People should stop using digital devices.
Paper books are more expensive than e-books.
Screens are always worse than paper for every purpose.
questions.explanation: 要約は本文の主張を一文でまとめ、具体例や言いすぎ（always・every）は入れない。

questions.prompt: 次の英文の内容を、日本語40字以内で要約せよ。
questions.explanation: 要約では、具体例や数字は省き、筆者の言いたいことを一文にまとめる。
questions.sentence: Many people believe that talent decides success. However, research on experts shows that years of focused practice, with clear goals and feedback, matter much more. Talent may help at first, but practice is what makes the difference in the end.

written.modelAnswer: 成功を決めるのは才能よりも、目標とフィードバックのある長年の練習である。

rubric.point: 「才能より練習」という対比をとらえている
練習の条件（目標・フィードバック・集中）にふれている
40字以内で、具体例を入れずにまとめている

questions.prompt: 下の英文の主語（文の主部）は？
questions.sentence: What surprised me most was the fact that nobody noticed the mistake.
questions.explanation: What surprised me most（私をいちばん驚かせたこと）が名詞節の主語で、動詞は was。

questions.prompt: 下の英文の意味として最も適切なものは？
questions.sentence: What she said was not as simple as I had expected.
choices: 彼女が言ったことは、思っていたほど簡単ではなかった。
彼女は、それが思ったより簡単だと言った。
彼女は簡単なことしか言わなかった。
彼女が言ったので、それは簡単になった。
questions.explanation: not as 形容詞 as I had expected＝「思っていたほど〜ではない」。主語は What she said。

questions.prompt: 下線の it が指すものは？
questions.sentence: I found it useful to keep a diary in English.
choices: to keep a diary in English
questions.explanation: 形式主語 it の真主語は to 以下（to keep a diary in English）。

questions.prompt: 下の英文の意味として最も適切なものは？
questions.sentence: Not until he finished the book did he realize the truth.
choices: その本を読まなかったので、彼は真実に気づかなかった。
その本を読み終えて初めて、彼は真実に気づいた。
彼は真実に気づいたので、本を読むのをやめた。
彼はその本を読み終えるまで、真実に気づいていた。
questions.explanation: Not until 〜 did S V（倒置）＝「〜して初めてSはVした」。It was not until 〜 that … と同じ意味。

questions.prompt: 下の英文で、that 以下の節が修飾している語は？
questions.sentence: Many people find it difficult to accept the idea that failure is part of learning.
questions.explanation: the idea that 〜 は同格の that 節で「〜という考え」。

questions.prompt: このお知らせの内容と合うものは？
questions.sentence:

questions.sentence:
City Library Summer Event

questions.prompt: グラフから言えることとして最も適切なものは？
choices: E-book users were more than paper book users in 2020.
Paper book users increased every year.
The number of e-book users more than doubled from 2020 to 2024.

questions.prompt: 2つのメールから分かることは？
questions.sentence:

choices: 会議は火曜日に変更された。
会議の場所が変わった。
会議は水曜日のままである。
questions.explanation: 1通目は水曜日の会議の案内、2通目で Tuesday に変更（Room 5 は同じ）。複数の資料は、あとの情報で前の情報が更新されていないかを確かめる。

questions.prompt: Kenta の条件に合う選択肢は？
questions.sentence: Kenta is planning a trip with his friends. Option A: a two-day camping trip by the lake (cost: 8,000 yen, bring your own tent). questions.explanation: 条件は「泊まる（2日）」かつ「1万円未満」。A は2日で8,000円。B は日帰り、C は15,000円。

questions.prompt: Option A に参加するときに必要なことは？
questions.sentence: Kenta is planning a trip with his friends. Option A: a two-day camping trip by the lake (cost: 8,000 yen, bring your own tent). choices: テントを自分で持っていく。

choices: Option C がいちばん安い。

questions.prompt: 筆者の主張として最も適切なものは？
questions.sentence: Some argue that technology makes us lonelier, because people spend more time looking at screens than talking face to face. Yet this view overlooks how technology also allows people who are isolated—by distance, illness, or shyness—to form communities they could never have joined before. The question, then, is not whether technology connects or isolates us, but how we choose to use it.
choices: 対面で話すことはもう必要ない。
技術は孤立した人だけを救う。
技術がつながりを生むか孤立を生むかは、使い方しだいである。
技術は人を孤独にする。
questions.explanation: Some argue… Yet… The question, then, is not A but B の流れ。筆者の主張は最後の not whether … but how we choose to use it。

questions.prompt: overlooks の意味に最も近いものは？
questions.sentence: Some argue that technology makes us lonelier, because people spend more time looking at screens than talking face to face. Yet this view overlooks how technology also allows people who are isolated—by distance, illness, or shyness—to form communities they could never have joined before. The question, then, is not whether technology connects or isolates us, but how we choose to use it.
questions.explanation: overlook は「見落とす」。文脈：技術が孤立した人をつなぐ面を見落としている。

questions.prompt: —by distance, illness, or shyness— が説明しているものは？
questions.sentence: Some argue that technology makes us lonelier, because people spend more time looking at screens than talking face to face. Yet this view overlooks how technology also allows people who are isolated—by distance, illness, or shyness—to form communities they could never have joined before. The question, then, is not whether technology connects or isolates us, but how we choose to use it.
choices: 人が孤立している理由
questions.explanation: isolated（孤立した）の原因を具体的に挙げている挿入句。

questions.prompt: 本文の論理展開として最も適切なものは？
questions.sentence: Some argue that technology makes us lonelier, because people spend more time looking at screens than talking face to face. Yet this view overlooks how technology also allows people who are isolated—by distance, illness, or shyness—to form communities they could never have joined before. The question, then, is not whether technology connects or isolates us, but how we choose to use it.
choices: 歴史的な経過を時系列で説明している。
具体例を並べたあと、結論を保留している。
2つの意見を比べて、多数派を支持している。
一般的な意見を紹介し、その見落としを指摘して、問いを立て直している。
questions.explanation: Some argue（一般論）→ Yet（反論・見落とし）→ The question, then, is not … but …（問いの立て直し）。

questions.prompt: 下の英文の下線部（The question, then, is not whether technology connects or isolates us, but how we choose to use it.）を和訳せよ。
questions.explanation: not A but B（AではなくB）と whether（〜かどうか）、how（どのように〜か）の名詞節を正しく訳す。
questions.sentence: Some argue that technology makes us lonelier, because people spend more time looking at screens than talking face to face. Yet this view overlooks how technology also allows people who are isolated—by distance, illness, or shyness—to form communities they could never have joined before. The question, then, is not whether technology connects or isolates us, but how we choose to use it.

written.modelAnswer: したがって問題は、技術が私たちをつなぐのか孤立させるのかではなく、私たちがそれをどのように使うことを選ぶのかということである。

rubric.point: not A but B を「AではなくB」と訳している
whether … or … を「…か…か」と訳している
how we choose to use it を「どのように使うことを選ぶか」と訳している
then を「したがって・それでは」として訳している

questions.prompt: 接頭辞 "un-" を付けて反対の意味になる語は？
questions.explanation: "un-" は否定：unhappy, unable, unknown。unite / union の "uni-" は「1つ」。

questions.prompt: "decide"（決める）の名詞形は？
questions.explanation: -sion で名詞。decisive は形容詞（決定的な）、decidedly は副詞。

questions.prompt: "-able" の意味から考えて、"readable" の意味は？
choices: 読みやすい（読むことができる）
questions.explanation: "-able" は「〜できる」。readable, washable, predictable。

questions.prompt: "hypothesis" の意味は？
questions.explanation: 論文・評論の頻出語。複数形は hypotheses。evidence＝証拠、bias＝偏見。

questions.prompt: "inevitable" の意味は？
questions.explanation: in-（否定）＋ evitable（避けられる）。"an inevitable result"＝避けられない結果。

questions.prompt: "phenomenon" の意味は？
questions.explanation: 複数形は phenomena。natural phenomena＝自然現象。

questions.prompt: I will call you when he ( ) home.
questions.explanation: 時・条件を表す副詞節（when / if 〜）の中では、未来のことも現在形で表す。
commonMistakes: 未来だから will come を選ぶ

questions.prompt: He said that he ( ) tired.
questions.explanation: 主節が過去（said）なので、従属節も過去に合わせる（時制の一致）。

questions.prompt: I don’t know if it ( ) tomorrow.（明日雨が降るかどうか）
questions.explanation: この if 節は know の目的語になる名詞節（〜かどうか）。名詞節では未来のことは will を使う。副詞節との区別がポイント。
commonMistakes: 副詞節と同じように現在形にする

questions.prompt: He must ( ) the train. He isn’t here yet.
questions.explanation: must have p.p.＝〜したにちがいない（過去への確信）。

questions.prompt: You should have told me.の意味は？
choices: 私に言うべきだったのに（言わなかった）
私に言ったにちがいない
私に言ったかもしれない
questions.explanation: should have p.p.＝〜すべきだったのに（しなかった）。過去の行為への後悔・非難。

questions.prompt: She can’t have said such a thing.の意味は？
choices: 彼女がそんなことを言ったはずがない
彼女はそんなことを言ったかもしれない
彼女はそんなことを言えない
彼女はそんなことを言うべきではなかった
questions.explanation: cannot have p.p.＝〜したはずがない。must have p.p. の反対。

questions.prompt: The baby was taken care ( ) by her aunt.
questions.explanation: 群動詞 take care of の受動態は of を残し、その後に by。
commonMistakes: of を落としてしまう

questions.prompt: I was spoken ( ) by a stranger.
questions.explanation: speak to の受動態 be spoken to by 〜。

questions.prompt: They say that he is rich. と同じ意味の文は？
choices: He is said to be rich.
questions.explanation: It is said that 〜 / 主語 + is said to 〜 に書きかえられる。

questions.prompt: This car is superior ( ) that one.
questions.explanation: ラテン比較級（superior, inferior, senior, junior, prefer）は than ではなく to を使う。

questions.prompt: No other mountain in Japan is as high as Mt. Fuji. と同じ意味の文は？
choices: Mt. Fuji is the highest mountain in Japan.
No mountain is higher than other mountains.
Mt. Fuji is not as high as other mountains.
Mt. Fuji is higher than all the mountains in the world.
questions.explanation: 「ほかのどの〜も…ほど〜ない」は最上級と同じ意味。比較級 Mt. Fuji is higher than any other mountain in Japan. も同じ。

questions.prompt: She plays ( ) piano very well.
questions.explanation: 楽器を演奏する play には the を付ける。スポーツ（play tennis）には付けない。

questions.prompt: I go to school by ( ) bus.
questions.explanation: 交通手段の by の後は無冠詞（by bus, by train）。

questions.prompt: I saw a cat. ( ) cat was black.
questions.explanation: 一度話題にした名詞を再び指すときは the。初めて出すときは a / an。

questions.prompt: 次の文から推測できることは？
questions.sentence: Ken kept typing for hours. When he finally looked up, the coffee on his desk had gone cold. He had not taken a single sip.
choices: ケンは仕事にとても集中していた
ケンはすぐ席を立った
ケンはコーヒーが嫌いだ
questions.explanation: コーヒーに手をつけず冷めた → 何かに没頭していた、と推測できる。書かれていることから一歩だけ推論する。

questions.prompt: 次の文の筆者の態度として最も適切なものは？
questions.sentence: The new app may save us time, but we should be careful about how much personal data it collects.
choices: 技術の歴史を紹介しているだけ
新しい技術に慎重な態度
新しい技術に全面的に賛成
技術にまったく関心がない
questions.explanation: "may" "but we should be careful" など、利点を認めつつ注意をうながす表現から慎重な態度を読み取る。

questions.prompt: 講義の一部：「Today, I’ll talk about three reasons why bees are important. First, ...」この講義で次に話される内容として最も適切なものは？
choices: ハチが重要である理由の1つ目
questions.explanation: 長い説明・講義は最初に「話の構成（three reasons）」が示されることが多い。First, Second, Finally などの目印で整理しながら聞く。

questions.prompt: 講義を聞いてメモを取るとき、最も効果的な方法は？
choices: 聞こえた英語をすべて書く
数字・固有名詞・つなぎの言葉（however, so など）を中心に、短く書く
知らない単語だけ書く
questions.explanation: 全部書こうとすると聞き逃す。話の構成と要点、逆接・結論の合図に注目する。

questions.prompt: "Check it out." は自然な発音ではどう聞こえる？
choices: チェッカウト・イット
チェック・イット・アウト
questions.explanation: 子音と母音がつながる「連結（リエゾン）」と、t の音の変化・脱落が起きる。

questions.prompt: "want to" が会話でよく変化した形は？
questions.explanation: want to → wanna、going to → gonna、got to → gotta。くだけた会話で起こる音の変化。
